title: Setting boundaries when you are covering for colleagues
summary: How to say what you can and cannot take on, without feeling guilty.
body: Covering for a colleague who is away is often a good thing to do. But extra work with no extra time is not sustainable.
Before agreeing, ask: what can I stop or delay to make room? Name the trade-off out loud: “I can take this on if X moves to next week.”
Agree an end date or a review date. “Until the end of the month, then let’s look again” is easier to accept than “for now”.
If you are asked to cover something you have not been trained for, say so and ask who can show you the basics.
